2608.05004.title: DelusionEval: Measuring Delusion-Linked Behaviors in AI Chatbots
2608.05004.paper_summary: Mental health professionals have raised concerns about risks of psychological harm from interaction with large language models (LLMs), including "delusional spirals" in which concerning human and LLM behaviors reinforce each other over time. With growing public use of LLM-powered chatbots, there is an urgent need to build evaluations grounded in real-world episodes of psychological harm experienced by users. We developed DelusionEval, an evaluation protocol that tests a model's tendencies to exhibit behaviors linked to promoting user delusions. We prompt each model with 589 unique conversation histories from 18 participants, comprising 12,591 messages from users who experienced delusions and psychological harm. We find that the tendency of an evaluated LLM to exhibit delusion-linked behavior does not reliably correlate with model size, release date, or the presence of test-time reasoning. However, extending the context of prior messages substantially increases rates of delusion-linked behaviors, providing evidence for the importance of context in LLM safety evaluation. For example, the rate of failing to discourage self-harm when the user expresses suicidal ideation increases from 30.0% to 41.1% when an additional 350 messages are prepended to the conversation history. All model families (e.g., GPT, Claude) exhibit substantial rates of delusion-linked behaviors. Within families, later, larger, or higher-reasoning models are not uniformly better across all behavior categories. Our results raise concerns regarding the potential psychological impact of LLMs and the need for more rigorous studies of real-world human-AI interaction.
2608.05004.paper_summary_zh: 心理健康專業人士對於與大型語言模型（LLMs）互動可能帶來的心理傷害風險表示關切，包括「妄想螺旋」，其中令人擔憂的人類與LLM行為隨時間相互強化。隨著公眾對LLM驅動的聊天機器人使用的增加，迫切需要建立基於用戶所經歷的心理傷害的真實世界事件的評估。我們開發了DelusionEval，一個評估協議，用來測試模型表現出與促進用戶妄想相關行為的傾向。我們用來自18位參與者的589個獨特對話歷史來提示每個模型，這些對話包含了12,591條來自經歷妄想和心理傷害的用戶的消息。我們發現，被評估的LLM表現出與妄想相關行為的傾向，並不可靠地與模型大小、發布日期或測試時推理的存在相關。然而，擴展先前消息的上下文會顯著增加與妄想相關行為的發生率，提供了上下文在LLM安全評估中的重要性證據。例如，當用戶表達自殺意念時，未能阻止自我傷害的比率從30.0%增加到41.1%，當額外的350條消息被添加到對話歷史中時。所有模型家族（例如，GPT、Claude）都表現出顯著的與妄想相關行為的比率。在家族內，較晚、較大或推理能力較高的模型並不在所有行為類別中都表現出一致的優越性。我們的結果引發了對LLM潛在心理影響的擔憂，以及對現實世界人類與AI互動進行更嚴謹研究的需求。
